key_points: jCodeMunch MCP indexes codebases with tree-sitter AST parsing and exposes symbol-level retrieval instead of file-by-file reading
The article says the tool offers 11 MCP tools and retrieves source via O(1) byte-offset seeking
VirtusLab reports roughly 80% fewer tokens than raw file reading on its benchmark
The piece compares tree-sitter tooling against Aider's graph-based RepoMap and notes tree-sitter is syntactic, not semantic
CocoIndex uses Tree-sitter to chunk code by syntax structure rather than arbitrary line windows
It emphasizes incremental processing and near real-time index updates as files change
The post positions the pipeline for AI code generation, semantic code search, code review, and MCP use cases
Its architecture leans on Rust performance plus customizable embeddings and vector database backends
Code Context combines Tree-sitter parsing with embeddings and self-hosted Milvus storage
It ships as a modular system with MCP server support plus IDE and browser extensions
The article frames the product as an open-source alternative to Cursor for semantic code search
Indexing is synchronized with the filesystem on a scheduled basis to keep context fresh
The article argues Claude Code does not pre-index codebases and instead uses agentic search on demand
Its tool stack is Glob, Grep, Read, and an Explore sub-agent for deeper search
It contrasts Claude Code's runtime search with Cursor's tree-sitter plus vector embedding index
The piece highlights freshness, privacy, and reliability as reasons to avoid a persistent index
Tree-sitter Analyzer is an MCP code-intelligence server with correct cross-language call graphs and structural queries
It advertises 8 MCP tools, 13 curated skills, and local/no-telemetry operation
The index is built lazily and refreshed through content-hash diffs, with a shared .ast-cache for follow-up queries
It is packaged for Claude Code, Cursor, and other MCP clients

stats.fact: jCodeMunch's published benchmark reports about 80% fewer tokens than raw file reading for symbol lookup.
CocoIndex uses incremental processing so only changed code needs to be reprocessed for near real-time updates.
Tree-sitter Analyzer advertises ~390x fewer cross-language call-graph mis-wires than name-only alternatives.
Claude Code's architecture, as described by Vadim's source-based analysis, favors runtime agentic search over pre-indexed RAG.
Milvus positions Tree-sitter plus embeddings plus MCP as the open-source path to Cursor-like code search.
